Although tempered by the low incidence of nearby astrophysical candidates, the most ambitious designs for deci-Hz detectors could detect such signals out to distances of ~250 Mpc, possibly at a rate of 0.3 per year. Additional numerical modeling is required to refine these rate estimates, however. We also demonstrate that proposed deci-Hz GW observation missions, even without confident single-source detections, could be used to provide information about the population of astrophysical candidates and, in particular, constrain the initial mass function of very massive stars.

papers.title: Epipolar-Constrained Graph Representation Learning for Geometric Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: We investigate geometry-aware graph representation learning for relative camera pose estimation using epipolar-constrained graph structures. Relative camera pose is commonly estimated from matched image correspondences that satisfy the epipolar constraint; however, identifying geometrically consistent correspondences under varying imaging conditions remains challenging. We employ an existing detector-free transformer architecture to establish correspondences between image pairs and construct a correspondence graph whose topology is guided by epipolar geometry. Initially, each node is connected to its (k) nearest neighbours based on spatial distance. The resulting graph is subsequently pruned using an initial estimate of the Essential Matrix, distinguishing the proposed formulation from conventional graph representations based primarily on heuristic spatial neighbourhoods. The graph learning module aggregates relational information between nodes into a graph-level representation that encodes the geometric context of the correspondences. This representation is passed to a pose regression network to estimate the relative camera rotation and translation. The model is trained across standard and wide baselines using a weighted objective that combines pose regression, scale consistency, heading consistency, and spectral properties of the pose parameters. Experimental graph analyses demonstrate that epipolar-guided edge pruning reduces graph connectivity by more than 90\% while retaining all correspondence nodes. Further spectral analyses characterize the effects of graph sparsification and injected outliers on learned graph representations.

papers.title: WHBench: Evaluating Frontier LLMs with Expert-in-the-Loop Validation on Women's Health Topics
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for medical guidance, but women's health remains under-evaluated in benchmark design. We present the Women's Health Benchmark (WHBench), a targeted evaluation suite of 47 expert-crafted scenarios across 10 women's health topics, designed to expose clinically meaningful failure modes including outdated guidelines, unsafe omissions, dosing errors, and equity-related blind spots. We evaluate 22 models using a 23-criterion rubric spanning clinical accuracy, completeness, safety, communication quality, instruction following, equity, uncertainty handling, and guideline adherence, with safety-weighted penalties and server-side score recalculation. Across 3,102 attempted responses (3,100 scored), no model mean performance exceeds 75 percent; the best model reaches 72.1 percent. Even top models show low fully correct rates and substantial variation in harm rates. Inter-rater reliability is moderate at the response label level but high for model ranking, supporting WHBench utility for comparative system evaluation while highlighting the need for expert oversight in clinical deployment. WHBench provides a public, failure-mode-aware benchmark to track safer and more equitable progress in womens health AI.

papers.title: From $α$ decay to cluster decay: an extreme case of transfer learning
papers.abstract: When training data are limited, data-driven models are especially vulnerable to optimization-related fluctuations from random initialization and to sampling-induced bias from insufficient training data. We address both challenges with transfer learning (TL): deep neural networks (DNNs) are first pretrained on $α$ decay half-lives and then fine-tuned on a small cluster decay dataset. The pretraining stage provides a physically informed initialization that stabilizes optimization, while transferred global decay systematics regularize the fit and reduce sensitivity to training set composition. Despite extreme data sparsity, the resulting models accurately predict cluster decay half-lives for parent nuclei from $^{221}$Fr to $^{242}$Cm. We further quantify how initialization and sample selection affect predictive accuracy and robustness, demonstrating that TL enables stable and reliable learning in the small-sample regime.

papers.title: Motivic local density of isolated surface singularities
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to compute the motivic local density of an isolated algebraic surface singularity, in order to explain its link with algebraic multiplicity. In this context, we can use an additional data: the inner rate related to the bilipschitz geometry of the singularity, as studied by A. Belotto da Silva, L. Fantini and A. Pichon.

papers.title: Gravitational-lensing-modulated leptonic CP violation
papers.abstract: The discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos has recently prompted interest in the role of gravity in neutrino flavor conversion. In this work, we investigate the gravity-modulated CP violation (CPV) in neutrino oscillations in the Reissner--Nordström and Hayward spacetimes. Employing analytical and numerical methods, we reveal the interplay among the CPV, the properties of neutrinos, and the space-time. The shapes of the flavor-oscillation curves show that CPV signals encode both space-time geometry and mass ordering, and that the imprints of $m_l$ are intrinsically correlated with the singular versus nonsingular structure of the background metric. In particular, our finding demonstrate that the CPV observables exceed the limitation that, in asymptotically flat space-time, gravity neither damps nor amplifies neutrino-oscillation amplitudes.

papers.title: Towards Reliable Local Security Agents: Verifiable Post-Training for Linux Privilege Escalation
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly important in security, yet leading systems are typically closed-source and cloud-hosted, limiting reproducibility and their use with sensitive data. This creates a need for small, local models that can perform security tasks under strict resource constraints, though effective methods for developing them remain underexplored. In this paper, we address this gap by proposing a two-stage post-training recipe that turns a small local language model into a security agent. To this end, we focus on Linux privilege escalation as a representative setting to systematically study the training of local models, as the task is automatically verifiable and requires multi-step interactive reasoning. Using an experimental setup that mitigates benchmark leakage, we post-train a small 4B model in two stages: supervised fine-tuning on traces from procedural privilege-escalation environments, followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. On a held-out benchmark of 12 Linux privilege-escalation scenarios, supervised fine-tuning nearly doubles the baseline success rate under a tight budget of 20 interaction rounds, and subsequent reinforcement learning improves our model, PrivEsc-LLM 4B, to 93.3% success, ahead of all other evaluated models that fit a single consumer GPU. At the same time, its expected inference cost per successful escalation is more than 80x lower than that of Claude Opus 4.7. Our findings show that small local models can be adapted to complex security tasks. We document the challenges involved and offer guidance for transferring this recipe to other settings.

papers.title: A Correlated Route to Antiferromagnetic Spintronics
papers.abstract: Antiferromagnets are attractive for spintronics owing to their vanishing net magnetization and ultrafast spin dynamics, yet their spin-compensated electronic structure has long confined them to passive roles. Here we identify a symmetry selection rule that overcomes this limitation: in a collinear antiferromagnet, a spin-polarized dc charge current requires the simultaneous breaking of particle--hole symmetry and of the equivalence between the two magnetic sublattices, either one alone leaving the polarization identically zero. We demonstrate the rule in the doped antiferromagnetic Hubbard model within dynamical mean-field theory: doping and a uniform magnetic field each break one of the two symmetries, and electronic correlations convert the resulting asymmetries into a sizable, field-tunable polarization of the charge current. The polarization is largest deep in the ordered phase and reverses sign at an emergent compensation point, set by the hierarchy of spin-dependent scattering rates and not dictated by symmetry, at which the dominant conducting spin species is interchanged. In correlated altermagnetic Hubbard models, the same two symmetries are broken structurally, by the sublattice-alternating hopping pattern: the field-driven mechanism identified here and the altermagnetic one are two realizations of a single selection rule. Electronic correlations thus emerge as an active ingredient for spintronics in structurally conventional collinear antiferromagnets.

papers.title: Gradual emergence of temporal structures depending on the distance between neighboring callers in natural habitat of male treefrogs
papers.abstract: Collective behavior, such as in-phase and anti-phase synchronizations in acoustic animals, is one of the most striking examples of self-organization in animal communication. However, understanding how synchronization emerges in natural environments has been limited by the difficulty of tracking multiple callers simultaneously in the wild. Here, we quantified spatio-temporal frequency characteristics in the choruses of wild treefrogs by combining large-scale sound-imaging and microphone-array systems. First, we performed field recordings by combining the sound-imaging system (25-66 units of sound-imaging devices) and microphone-array system (16-24 channels of microphones) between 2021 and 2023. Second, we analyzed the video and audio data and quantified the call frequency, call timing, and caller position of each male across 11 choruses comprising 66 males in total. Based on this dataset, we have shown that synchronized behavior gradually emerges between neighboring callers depending on their distances even when the call frequency and chorus density moderately vary. These findings provide field-based evidence for how local acoustic interactions generate collective temporal order in animal groups.

papers.title: Bridging Scene Generation and Planning: Driving with World Model via Unifying Vision and Motion Representation
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving aims to generate safe and plausible planning policies from raw sensor inputs, and constructing an effective scene representation is a critical challenge. Driving world models have shown great potential in learning rich representations by predicting the future evolution of a driving scene. However, existing driving world models primarily focus on visual scene representation, and motion representation is not explicitly designed to be planner-shared and inheritable, leaving a schism between the optimization of visual scene generation and the requirements of precise motion planning. We present WorldDrive, a holistic framework that couples scene generation and real-time planning via unifying vision and motion representation. We first introduce a Trajectory-aware Driving World Model, which conditions on a trajectory vocabulary to enforce consistency between visual dynamics and motion intentions, enabling the generation of diverse and plausible future scenes conditioned on a specific trajectory. We transfer the vision and motion encoders to a downstream Multi-modal Planner, ensuring the driving policy operates on mature representations pre-optimized by scene generation. A simple interaction between motion representation, visual representation, and ego status can generate high-quality, multi-modal trajectories. Furthermore, to exploit the world model's foresight, we propose a Future-aware Rewarder, which distills future latent representation from the frozen world model to evaluate and select optimal trajectories in real-time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that WorldDrive achieves leading planning performance among vision-only methods while maintaining high-fidelity action-controlled video generation capabilities.

papers.title: FAR-Drive: Frame-AutoRegressive Video Generation for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Despite rapid progress in autonomous driving, interactive simulation remains a fundamental bottleneck. Existing closed-loop simulators generate video in multi-frame chunks to maintain short-term stability, yet this coarse granularity weakens the fine-grained interaction between agent actions and visual dynamics. Directly adopting frame-level autoregressive generation restores this interaction but sharply intensifies two challenges: long-horizon consistency and autoregressive stability under iterative self-conditioning. In this paradigm, each step is a single action-conditioned update, which also imposes strict low-latency demands since every step requires a full inference pass. In this work, we propose FAR-Drive, a Frame-level AutoRegressive video generation framework for autonomous driving, which integrates a multi-view diffusion transformer with fine-grained structured control to produce geometrically consistent multi-camera videos. At the core of our framework, we design a two-stage training strategy: (i) adaptive reference-horizon conditioning, which expands the temporal conditioning window for long-horizon consistency, and (ii) blend-forcing training, which gradually shifts from ground-truth to self-conditioned inputs to improve autoregressive stability. We further integrate system-level inference optimizations to satisfy the low-latency constraint. Experiments on nuScenes show that our method achieves state-of-the-art results among autoregressive driving video generation methods while keeping sub-second latency on a single GPU.

papers.title: Toroidal families and averages of $L$-functions, II: cubic moments
papers.abstract: Generalizing our previous work on ``toroidal averages'', we study the average of special values of $L$-functions of the form $L(1/2,χ^a)L(1/2,χ^b)L(1/2,χ^c)$ for integers $a$, $b$ and $c$, where $χ$ varies over Dirichlet characters of a given prime modulus. We highlight connections with estimates for bilinear forms of trace functions and with bounds for the number of solutions of monoidal equations in three variables in small boxes over finite fields.

papers.title: Memorization capacity of deep ReLU neural networks characterized by width and depth
papers.abstract: This paper studies the memorization capacity of deep neural networks with ReLU activation. Specifically, we investigate the minimal size of such networks to memorize any $N$ data points in the unit ball with pairwise separation distance $δ$ and labels from a finite set of size $C$. Most prior studies characterize the memorization capacity by the number of parameters or neurons. We extend these results by constructing ReLU networks with adjustable width $W$ and depth $L$ satisfying $W^2L^2\log W=\mathcal{O}(N(\log(δ^{-1})+\log C))$ that can memorize any such dataset. We also establish width-depth lower bounds that depend explicitly on $δ$ and $C$ for networks capable of memorizing all such datasets. When $\log(δ^{-1})\asymp\log N$, our construction achieves $W^2L^2\asymp N$ for suitable choices of width and depth. This order is optimal if $\log C\asymp\log N$, and optimal up to logarithmic factors if $\log C=o(\log N)$.

papers.title: Improved Pion-Kaon Identification in Heavy-Ion Collisions with a Two-Dimensional Transformation
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of charged pions and kaons is essential for precision measurements in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but becomes increasingly challenging at intermediate and high transverse momentum because of the increasing overlap of the TPC and TOF particle identification responses. In this work, we quantitatively benchmark a two-dimensional shift-and-rotation PID procedure that combines the $nσ_π$ and mass-squared $(m^{2})$ information. The benchmark is performed using Au+Au collision events generated with the AMPT model, where the detector response is modeled using $p_{T}$-dependent PID parameters extracted from STAR data. Since the true particle identities and input yields are known in AMPT but are not used during the reconstruction, the procedure can be evaluated through a direct closure test that is not possible with experimental data alone. The two-dimensional procedure is compared with a reference one-dimensional method consisting of an $|nσ_π|<$ 3 preselection followed by a Gaussian fit to the $m^{2}$ distribution. While both methods perform well when pion and kaon PID responses are well separated, the two-dimensional procedure provides improved yield closure as the PID distributions increasingly overlap at high $p_{T}$. The reconstructed-to-input yield ratio remains within 2\% of unity up to $p_T =$ 3 GeV/$c$, whereas the reference one-dimensional procedure shows a larger deviation. Reaction-plane $v_{2}$ closure tests show that both the reference one-dimensional and two-dimensional PID procedures reproduce the AMPT input $v_{2}$ within the statistical uncertainties over the studied $p_{T}$ range. These results demonstrate that the two-dimensional procedure substantially improves the high-$p_{T}$ yield reconstruction without introducing a detectable bias in the extracted $v_{2}$ under the STAR-like detector response considered here.

papers.title: One-point energy correlator for deep inelastic scattering at small $x$
papers.abstract: We derive the expressions for the one-point energy correlator (OPEC) in deep inelastic scattering in the high-energy (small-$x$) limit within the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework. The OPEC is computed as a function of the angle between the energy flow and the target proton or nucleus, enabling a systematic exploration of different momentum scales in the scattering process. Owing to the momentum sum rule, the dependence on fragmentation functions cancels, leaving the dipole amplitude as the only nonperturbative input. As a result, the OPEC provides a sensitive and promising probe of gluon saturation dynamics at small $x$. We present numerical results for representative kinematic configurations relevant to the future Electron--Ion Collider, demonstrating sizable nuclear suppression effects within the CGC framework and highlighting the consistency of this observable with predictions from gluon saturation.

papers.title: Evaluating and Understanding Scheming Propensity in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: As frontier language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents pursuing complex, long-term objectives, there is increased risk of scheming: agents covertly pursuing misaligned goals. Prior work has focused on showing agents are capable of scheming, but their propensity to scheme in realistic scenarios remains underexplored. To understand when agents scheme, we decompose scheming incentives into agent factors and environmental factors. We develop realistic settings allowing us to systematically vary these factors, each with scheming opportunities for agents that pursue instrumentally convergent goals such as self-preservation, resource acquisition, and goal-guarding. Across 11 frontier models and four scenarios, we find almost no scheming despite high environmental incentives, and show this is unlikely to be explained by verbalized evaluation awareness. While inserting adversarially-designed prompt snippets that encourage agency and goal-directedness into an agent's system prompt can induce high scheming rates, snippets used in real agent scaffolds rarely do. In model organisms built with these snippets, scheming behavior is brittle: removing a single tool can drop the scheming rate from 59% to 3%. Increasing oversight can raise rather than deter scheming by up to 25%, an effect that depends on the wording of the oversight sentence and does not appear in a second scenario, where the sabotage itself is reviewed. These results suggest that scheming propensity should be reported per agent configuration rather than as a single rate. Our incentive decomposition enables such systematic measurement in settings relevant for deployment, which is necessary as agents are entrusted with increasingly consequential tasks.

papers.title: Mean-field games with rough common noise: the linear-quadratic case
papers.abstract: Motivated by mean-field games (MFG) with common noise on the one hand and pathwise stochastic control theory on the other, we formulate here a linear-quadratic (LQ) MFG with rough common noise, along with a satisfactory well-posedness theory for the linear-quadratic case. A novel Volterra-type (or mild) formulation allows to keep technical (rough-stochastic) consideration to a minimum. We derive a characterization of the optimal state and optimal control through a rough forward-backward SDE (rough FBSDE), and provide an existence and uniqueness result under the usual assumptions. Our theory is accompanied by stability estimates with respect to initial data and common noise while we also establish continuity of what we call the Itô-Lions-Lyons map for rough mean-field games. Finally, we discuss randomization of the rough common noise under appropriate conditions on the coefficients. When the latter is given by the Stratonovich lift of a Brownian motion independent of the idiosyncratic noise, we show that solutions of the rough LQ MFG coincide with those obtained by conditioning on the common noise.

papers.title: UniE2F: A Unified Diffusion Framework for Event-to-Frame Reconstruction with Video Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Event cameras excel at high-speed, low-power, and high-dynamic-range scene perception. However, as they fundamentally record only relative intensity changes rather than absolute intensity, the resulting data streams suffer from a significant loss of spatial information and static texture details. In this paper, we address this limitation by leveraging the generative prior of a pre-trained video diffusion model to reconstruct high-fidelity video frames from sparse event data. Specifically, we first establish a baseline model by directly applying event data as a condition to synthesize videos. Then, based on the physical correlation between the event stream and video frames, we further introduce the event-based inter-frame residual guidance to enhance the accuracy of video frame reconstruction. Furthermore, we extend our method to video frame interpolation and prediction in a zero-shot manner by modulating the reverse diffusion sampling process, thereby creating a unified event-to-frame reconstruction framework. Experimental results on real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms previous reconstruction approaches on most quantitative metrics and achieves superior qualitative results, while achieving competitive zero-shot performance compared with dedicated methods explicitly trained for interpolation and prediction tasks. We also refer the reviewers to the video demo contained in the supplementary material for video results. The code will be publicly available at https://github.com/CS-GangXu/UniE2F.

papers.title: Dispersive analysis of the $\boldsymbol{ϕ\to γπ^0 π^0}$ process
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of the radiative decay $ϕ\to γπ^0 π^0$ in a dispersive framework, where the two-pion subsystem undergoes strong final-state interactions that cover the $f_0(500)$ and $f_0(980)$ regions. We employ a coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omnès framework that allows for a consistent treatment of two scalar resonances and crossed-channel singularities induced by the Born and vector-meson exchanges. We explicitly verify the equivalence between the modified and standard Muskhelishvili-Omnès representations for vector-meson pole contributions when the isoscalar Omnès matrix is chosen asymptotically bounded, and we adopt the standard representation in decay kinematics. This yields, for the first time, a parameter-free dispersive prediction for the kaon Born rescattering, which provides a dominant contribution. To obtain a good fit to the KLOE and SND data, we employ a once-subtracted coupled-channel dispersion relation with heavier left-hand cut contributions and two unknown subtraction constants. The results demonstrate the consistency among the data for $ππ$ scattering, $γγ$ fusion, and $ϕ$ radiative decay, thereby validating the underlying dispersive formalism and the input used for the hadronic Omnès matrix and left-hand cuts.

papers.title: GPTZero: Robust Detection of LLM-Generated Texts
papers.abstract: While historical considerations surrounding text authenticity revolved primarily around plagiarism, the advent of large language models (LLMs) has introduced a new challenge: distinguishing human-authored from AI-generated text. This shift raises significant concerns, including the undermining of skill evaluations, the mass-production of low-quality content, and the proliferation of misinformation. Addressing these issues, we introduce GPTZero 5.0, a state-of-the-art industrial AI detection solution, offering reliable discernment between human and LLM-generated text. Our key contributions include: introducing a hierarchical, multi-task architecture enabling a flexible taxonomy of human and AI texts, setting a new state-of-the-art for AI detection accuracy on 11 independent third-party benchmarks and 18 writing domains, and achieving superior robustness to adversarial attacks and paraphrasing via multi-tiered automated red teaming. GPTZero offers accurate and explainable detection, and educates users on its responsible use, ensuring fair and transparent assessment of text.

papers.title: The Wasserstein gradient flow of the Sinkhorn divergence between Gaussian distributions
papers.abstract: We study the Wasserstein gradient flow of the Sinkhorn divergence when both the source and the target are Gaussian distributions. We prove the existence of a flow that stays in the class of Gaussian distributions, and is unique in the larger class of measures with strongly-concave and smooth log-densities. We prove that the flow globally converges toward the target measure when the source's covariance matrix is not singular, and provide counter-examples to global convergence when it is, giving a first answer to an open question raised in [Carlier et al. 2024, \S4.2]. When the covariance matrix of the source distribution commutes with that of the target, we derive more quantitative results that showcase exponential convergence toward the target when the source and the target share their support, but dropping to sublinear rates (O(t^{-1})) if the target is concentrated on a strict subspace of the source's support.

papers.title: W-SLDA Toolkit: A simulation platform for ultracold Fermi gases
papers.abstract: We present the W-SLDA Toolkit, a general-purpose software package for simulating ultracold Fermi gases within the framework of density functional theory and its time-dependent extensions. The toolkit enables fully microscopic studies of interacting superfluid systems across the BCS-BEC crossover, including spin-imbalanced configurations and arbitrary external geometries. It provides both static and time-dependent solvers capable of describing a broad range of phenomena in one-, two-, and three-dimensional settings. In addition, the toolkit incorporates functionality for solving the standard Bogoliubov-de~Gennes equations for fermions, extending its applicability to other physical systems such as superconductors. The code is implemented in C with GPU acceleration and is optimized for hybrid CPU/GPU execution on modern high-performance computing platforms. It ensures scalability on leadership-class supercomputers, enabling fully three-dimensional simulations with large atom numbers, and allows for direct benchmarks of ultracold-atom experimental setups. Its modular architecture facilitates straightforward extensions, user customization, and seamless interoperability with other scientific software frameworks. Furthermore, an extensive collection of practical usage examples is provided through the integrated \textit{reproducibility packs} functionality, ensuring transparency and reproducibility of computational results.

papers.title: MadSpace -- Event Generation for the Era of GPUs and ML
papers.abstract: MadSpace is a new modular phase-space and event-generation library written in C++ with native GPU support via CUDA and HIP. It provides a unified compute-graph-based framework for phase-space construction, adaptive and neural importance sampling, and event unweighting. It includes a wide range of mappings, from the standard MadGraph multi-channel phase space to optimized normalizing flows with analytic inverse transformations. All components operate on batches of events and support end-to-end on-device workflows. A high-level Python interface enables seamless integration with machine-learning libraries such as PyTorch.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo for Combinatorial Optimization
papers.abstract: Quantum computing offers an alternative paradigm for addressing combinatorial optimization problems compared to classical methods. However, despite recent hardware improvements, the execution of empirical quantum optimization experiments at scales known to be hard for state-of-the-art classical solvers is not yet in reach. In this work, we offer a different way to approach combinatorial optimization with near-term quantum computing. Motivated by the promising results observed in using quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QeMCMC) for approximating complicated probability distributions, we combine ideas of sampling from the device with QeMCMC together with warm-starting and parallel tempering, in the context of combinatorial optimization. We demonstrate empirically that our algorithm recovers the global optima for instances of the Maximum Independent Set problem (MIS) up to 117 decision variables using 117 qubits on IBM quantum hardware. We observe an indication of more favorable scaling relative to the tested classical MCMC methods on the chosen MIS instances. MIS is practically relevant across domains such as financial services and molecular biology. Although some MIS instances with a few hundred variables can be difficult for classical solvers, the instances studied here are solved efficiently by CPLEX.

papers.title: Beyond Success Rates: Trainability and Extractability for Offline GCRL
papers.abstract: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL) methods are typically benchmarked by the success rates of optimized hyperparameter configurations. However, success rate by itself does not provide information about the sensitivity of algorithms to hyperparameters for value learning or policy extraction, since an algorithm could obtain the same success rate across a wide range of hyperparameters, or might succeed only on specific settings. We study this phenomenon in the offline GCRL algorithms GCIQL, GCIVL, QRL, and CRL under a shared policy extractor, by constructing landscapes of interaction between the learning rate and policy extraction hyperparameters such as the temperature of advantage-weighted regression (AWR). These landscapes reveal large, task-dependent differences in hyperparameter sensitivity. On AntMaze-M, 59% of QRL configurations and 66% of CRL configurations achieve at least 90% of the method's best sampled success rate, compared with 3% for both GCIQL and GCIVL. On Cube and Scene, GCIQL and GCIVL instead attain higher success over broader hyperparameter regions than QRL and CRL. To interpret these differences, we analyze how reliably learned advantages rank actual goals from the same trajectory above random goals, and how strongly AWR concentrates policy updates on a small subset of transitions. Our findings indicate strongly differing behavior of these algorithms at policy-extraction time, even under the same success rates. Given these results, we argue that offline GCRL methods should be evaluated by both attainable success and the needed hyperparameter range to sustain it, complemented by post-hoc diagnostics to understand the signal used to train the policy. The overview and code are available at https://luh-ai.github.io/GCRL-Landscapes/ .

papers.title: Agentic AI-Empowered Dynamic Survey Framework
papers.abstract: Survey papers play a central role in synthesizing and organizing scientific knowledge, yet they are increasingly strained by the rapid growth of research output. As new work continues to appear after publication, surveys quickly become outdated, contributing to redundancy and fragmentation in the literature. We reframe survey writing as a long-horizon maintenance problem rather than a one-time generation task, treating surveys as living documents that evolve alongside the research they describe. We propose an agentic Dynamic Survey Framework that supports the continuous updating of existing survey papers by incrementally integrating new work while preserving survey structure and minimizing unnecessary disruption. Using a retrospective experimental setup, we demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively identifies and incorporates emerging research while preserving the coherence and structure of existing surveys, even over extended sequences of updates.

papers.title: On the distribution of multiplicative energy
papers.abstract: This paper extends the investigation of energy distribution in finite settings, building on results established in our earlier work. We analyze the distribution of multiplicative energies of different orders using Fourier-analytic methods. Our results provide new structural insights into energy phenomena in finite fields, complementing earlier discrete analyses. In the last section, as a corollary, we obtain a 'sum-multiplicative energy'-type result.

papers.title: GCD: GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling across Heterogeneous GCMs
papers.abstract: Climate downscaling of General Circulation Models (GCMs) is an ill-posed inverse problem, as GCM outputs and reanalysis fields arise from different dynamical systems and lack fine-scale temporal pairing. Supervised methods thus rely on synthetic degradations or model-specific adaptation, limiting generalization across heterogeneous GCMs. Zero-shot diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) avoids paired supervision by combining a high-resolution climate prior with inference-time constraints from coarse GCM inputs, but faces consistency and efficiency challenges. We propose GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling (GCD), which addresses these challenges with geographic conditioning, spectrally filtered measurement guidance, and distillation-accelerated Conjugate Gradient guidance. GCD reduces inference from 1,000 diffusion steps to 6 while maintaining consistency with the coarse GCM inputs. Across five heterogeneous GCMs, GCD achieves competitive 99th-percentile extreme-event accuracy and reconstructs plausible high-frequency tropical cyclone structures without model-specific retraining. Github: https://github.com/shawnvonbohr/GCD-Climate-Downscaling.git

papers.title: Mean-Field Learning for Storage Aggregation
papers.abstract: Distributed energy storage devices can be aggregated to provide operational flexibility for power systems. Their efficient integration into system-level optimization calls for an accurate and computationally tractable surrogate that jointly represents aggregate flexibility and operating costs. However, constructing such a surrogate is challenging due to device heterogeneity, nonconvex operating constraints, and high-dimensional power trajectories. To address these challenges, this paper develops a mean-field learning framework for storage aggregation. Using random-set expectations, we show that the joint representation of aggregate flexibility and operating costs converges almost surely to a deterministic convex mean-field limit. This limit provides a learning benchmark for storage aggregation, against which we bound the approximation error of any convex surrogate. These theoretical results motivate a convex virtual-battery surrogate with physically interpretable parameters. We learn these parameters through a bilevel optimization problem that matches the optimal values of the surrogate and the storage fleet when both respond to a set of price scenarios. We derive closed-form gradients to solve this problem efficiently. Case studies illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the framework's approximation accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to device heterogeneity.

papers.title: A Quantum Photonic Approach to Graph Coloring
papers.abstract: Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) is a quantum computational model that leverages linear optics to solve sampling problems believed to be classically intractable. Recent experimental breakthroughs have demonstrated quantum advantage using GBS, motivating its application to real-world combinatorial optimization problems. In this work, we reformulate the graph coloring problem as an integer programming problem using the independent set formulation. This enables the use of GBS to identify cliques in the complement graph, which correspond to independent sets in the original graph. Our method is benchmarked against classical heuristics and exact algorithms on two sets of instances: Erdős-Rényi random graphs and graphs derived from a smart-charging use case. The results demonstrate that GBS can provide competitive solutions, highlighting its potential as a quantum-enhanced heuristic for graph-based optimization.

papers.title: On the Fourier Mean Bodies of a Convex Body
papers.abstract: In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_pK$ of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $p>-1$, which have since become important objects in geometric tomography. In this paper, we study the Fourier transforms of the radial functions of $R_pK$. This leads to a new family of star-shaped sets $F_pK$, which we call the Fourier $p$th mean bodies of $K$. We prove Fourier inversion formulas connecting $R_pK$ and $F_pK$, realizing them as $p$-intersection bodies in the sense of A. Koldobsky. We develop the basic affine geometry of $F_pK$; this includes affine covariance and monotonicity properties. We give sufficient conditions for the compactness of $F_pK$ in terms of the decay of $|\widehat{χ_K}|^2$. We show that $F_pK$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for every $0<p\le1$. This range is sharp in general: already for the cube, $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not convex for $1<p<2$ and $n\geq 2,$ while $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not compact for $p\geq 2$. We further investigate the features Fourier mean bodies share with intersection bodies: we prove Hensley-type estimates for $F_pK$ when $K$ is isotropic and investigate an affine isoperimetric inequality.

papers.title: Realisation of a Protected Cat-Qutrit Manifold via Engineered Quantum Tunnelling
papers.abstract: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform.

papers.title: Exploration stabilizes learning dynamics and promotes cooperation in stochastic games
papers.abstract: Understanding and stabilizing collective learning dynamics is a central challenge in stochastic games. Although exploration is widely used in learning algorithms, its effects on the coupled dynamics of agents and their environment remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we derive analytical equations for entropy-regularized actor-critic learning in stochastic games by separating the timescales of value estimation and policy adaptation. Without exploration, the system preserves a weighted volume in the policy phase space, ruling out asymptotically stable fully mixed equilibria. We provide a unified characterization of exploration's effects on objective curvature, preference dynamics in log-ratio coordinates, and the forgetting of past action preferences. Exploration reduces local volume expansion and can stabilize learning dynamics. In a two-state Matching Pennies game, it suppresses chaotic learning and promotes convergence to a mixed equilibrium. In a Prisoner's Dilemma with environmental feedback, intermediate exploration eliminates the defective attractor and expands the basin of attraction of the cooperative equilibrium. Our findings reveal how exploration shapes collective behavior, informing the design of cooperative and resilient multi-agent systems.

papers.title: Associator Defects in Non-Unitary String-Nets
papers.abstract: We study obstructions to realizing fusion categories in physical Hilbert spaces by varying positive inner products on elementary fusion spaces. We introduce an associator defect to measure the smallest failure of recoupling maps to preserve the induced inner products in order to do so. By using a determinant identity from the pentagon equation, we prove that the minimum is attained and vanishes when the category is unitarizable. As an example, we compute the defect for the Yang-Lee category and its double, studying its behavior under stacking and passage to Drinfeld centers, which results in a Morita-invariant measure of bulk nonunitarity. We also obtain lower bounds for quantum-group categories with fusion multiplicities. Finally, we study how these obstructions appear in physical realizations of fusion. Under the stated assumptions on local splitting operations and coherent measurements, a positive defect imposes quantitative tradeoffs between implementation errors and operator norms. We also obtain bounds on the response to local perturbations. These results show how the failure of categorical unitarity will place quantitative constraints on physical realizations of potential fusion.

papers.title: Study of $CP$ violation in $Λ_b^0\rightarrow N^*M$ decays with the final-state rescattering mechanism
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the charmless nonleptonic two-body $Λ_b$ decays within the framework of final-state rescattering mechanism. Using this framework, we evaluate the relevant hadronic triangle diagrams by performing the loop integrations, retaining both their absorptive and dispersive parts. Based on the established formalism, we analyze the $Λ_b \to N^*(1535,1520)M$ decay processes with $M =K_S, K^*_0(700)$, $f_0(500,980), ρ(770), \bar{K}^{*0}$, $ϕ$, and predict various physical observables, such as their branching ratios, direct and partial-wave $CP$ asymmetries, as well as decay asymmetry parameters. These two-body decay processes are expected to contribute primarily to the subsequent four-body decay channels, such as $Λ_b^0 \to p\,π^-\,π^+\,π^-$, whose $CP$ asymmetry measurements will be accessible at the LHCb experiment.

papers.title: Grundy Values of Node-Kayles on Level-Regular Trees
papers.abstract: Node-Kayles is an impartial combinatorial game played on graphs, in which the two players alternately select a vertex and remove it together with all of its neighbours. By the Sprague--Grundy theorem, every position has a Grundy value that determines its outcome under optimal play. In this paper we study the Grundy values of Node-Kayles on level-regular trees $\T{a}$, $a=(a_1,\dots,a_d)$, in which every vertex at level $i-1$ has exactly $a_i$ children. We determine the Grundy values of all level-regular trees of depth at most two, show that $\G(\T{a})\le d+1$, and prove that $\G(\T{a})>0$ whenever $a_1a_2a_3$ is even, using an explicit mirror strategy. We prove a Leaf-Pair Lemma, which shows that the last branching parameter $a_d$ matters only through its parity, and a Twin Lemma for subgraphs that come in isomorphic pairs; as a consequence, $\G(\T{1,2k,s})=1$ for every $k\ge1$ and every finite sequence $s$. For trees containing a long run of ones, we give a general periodicity criterion: if the Grundy values of a tree with a pendant path of length $h$ are $34$-periodic on a finite window, then they are $34$-periodic for all larger $h$. This criterion extends to paths joining two fixed subtrees, and it explains the eventual periodicity of the families $\T{1^k,2}$ and $\T{2,1^k,2}$. We also show that, in this setting, eventual periodicity is equivalent to the boundedness of the Grundy values. Finally, supported by computations, we conjecture that the Grundy values are eventually periodic, with period $2$, in each branching parameter, and eventually periodic in the length of every run of ones.

papers.title: Polynomiality ideals, with applications to polynomial functors over free nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a unital commutative ring. For a monoidal category $C$ whose unit is a zero object, we introduce a descending filtration of the k-linearization of $C$ by two-sided ideals, called the polynomiality ideals: the $d$-th ideal encodes polynomiality of degree at most $d$ for functors from $C$ to $k$-modules. These ideals yield general criteria for the existence of polynomial functors of a given degree and for equivalences between the categories of polynomial functors of degree at most $d$ over different base categories. For Lawvere theories satisfying a mild condition, we identify the polynomiality ideals with powers of augmentation ideals of monoids; this identification makes the criteria computable by means of classical group ring theory. As the main application, we study polynomial functors over finitely generated free nilpotent groups, comparing them across nilpotency classes and polynomial degrees. We obtain refinements of results of Baues and Pirashvili in the case of class at most 2, recover several folklore results for free groups and free abelian groups, and establish a modular analogue formulated with dimension subgroups over a field of positive characteristic in place of the lower central series. Finally, we show that, in contrast to polynomial functors, analytic functors admit no analogous ideal in most cases.

papers.title: Prospect for measurement of CP-violating parameters of $B_s^0 \to ϕγ$ at the Tera Z factory
papers.abstract: $b \to sγ$ transition is a critical flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) process that could be used to probe CP violation (CPV) and new physics (NP). We quantify the anticipated precision for measuring $B_s^0 \to ϕγ$ at the CEPC Z pole operation, showing that the relative statistical uncertainty could be as low as 0.16\%, improved by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to existing measurements. Additionally, we perform a time-dependent analysis of the $B_s^0 \to ϕγ$ decay, accounting for $B_s^0/\bar{B}_s^0$ mixing extract the mixing-induced and CP-violating parameters $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}_{ϕγ}^Δ}$, $\boldsymbol{C_{ϕγ}}$ and $\boldsymbol{S_{ϕγ}}$. Using central value from LHCb measurement as input, we evaluate the anticipated accuracy of measurements of these parameters. The projected statistical uncertainties are $σ_{A_{ϕγ}^Δ{}^{\text{stat}}} = 0.021$, $σ_C^{\text{stat}} = 0.0092$ and $σ_S^{\text{stat}} = 0.0096$, and the systematic uncertainties are $σ_{A_{ϕγ}^Δ{}^{\text{syst}}} = 0.035$, $σ_C^{\text{syst}} = 0.0027$ and $σ_S^{\text{syst}} = 0.0064$. Furthermore, the 1$σ$ sensitivity boundaries for NP in this study are found to be $\mathcal{A}_{ϕγ}^Δ< -0.05$ or $\mathcal{A}_{ϕγ}^Δ> 0.15$, $\mathcal{C}_{ϕγ} < -0.02$ or $\mathcal{C}_{ϕγ} > 0.04$, and $\mathcal{S}_{ϕγ} < -0.04$ or $\mathcal{S}_{ϕγ} > 0.04$. We also conduct a relevant detector optimization study by establishing the correlation between the anticipated precision and the intrinsic resolution of the ECAL, as well as the performance of the PID system.

papers.title: Learning Generalizable Hand-Object Tracking from Synthetic Demonstrations
papers.abstract: We present a system for learning generalizable hand-object tracking controllers purely from synthetic data, without requiring any human demonstrations. Our approach makes two key contributions: (1) HOG, a highly efficient Hand-Object data generator that rapidly synthesizes diverse, large-scale, and uniformly distributed trajectories; and (2) HOT, a Hand-Object Tracker that bridges synthetic-to-physical transfer through reinforcement learning and interaction imitation learning. Our method extends to diverse object shapes and hand morphologies. HOT also enables cross-simulator transfer. Through extensive evaluations, we show that our approach enables dexterous hands to track challenging, long-horizon sequences including object re-arrangement and agile in-hand reorientation. These results represent a significant step toward scalable foundation controllers for manipulation that can learn entirely from simple, scalable synthetic data, breaking the data bottleneck that has long constrained progress in dexterous manipulation.

papers.title: CORE: Concept-Oriented Reinforcement for Bridging the Definition-Application Gap in Mathematical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often solve challenging math exercises yet fail to apply the concept right when the problem requires genuine understanding. Popular Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) pipelines reinforce final answers but provide little fine-grained conceptual signal, so models improve at pattern reuse rather than conceptual applications. We introduce CORE (Concept-Oriented REinforcement), an RL training framework that turns explicit concepts into a controllable supervision signal. Starting from a high-quality, low-contamination textbook resource that links verifiable exercises to concise concept descriptions, we run a sanity probe showing LLMs can restate definitions but fail concept-linked quizzes, quantifying the conceptual reasoning gap. CORE then (i) synthesizes concept-aligned quizzes, (ii) injects brief concept snippets during rollouts to elicit concept-primed trajectories, and (iii) reinforces conceptual reasoning via trajectory replacement after group failures, a lightweight forward-KL constraint that aligns unguided with concept-primed policies, or standard GRPO directly on concept-aligned quizzes. Across several models, CORE delivers consistent gains over vanilla and SFT baselines on both in-domain concept-exercise suites and diverse out-of-domain math benchmarks. CORE unifies direct training on concept-aligned quizzes and concept-injected rollouts under outcome regularization. It provides fine-grained conceptual supervision that bridges problem-solving competence and genuine conceptual reasoning, while remaining algorithm- and verifier-agnostic.

papers.title: AGN x-ray reflection spectroscopy with ML_MYTORUS: Neural posterior estimation with training on observation-driven parameter grids
papers.abstract: X-ray spectroscopy of active galactic nuclei (AGN) probes circumnuclear matter geometry. Many AGN show a narrow Fe K $α$ line at 6.4 keV and associated Compton-scattered continua in their x-ray spectra, due to primary continuum scattering in cold, neutral material far from the central supermassive black hole. We present a novel approach via Simulation-Based Inference with Neural Posterior Estimation (SBI-NPE) and train a machine learning neural network (ML NN) model based on $NuSTAR$ spectral fitting results from the literature, employing the physically motivated MYTORUS-decoupled model, which distinguishes line-of-sight from global equivalent neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm H,Z}$ vs. $N_{\rm H,S}$). To overcome the limitations of traditional frequentist fitting (e.g., lack of automation, reproducibility, computational cost), we implement normalizing flows and autoregressive networks to learn flexible posterior distributions from simulated spectra. From 34 $NuSTAR$ spectral fitting literature results, we simulate 34,000 spectra for both a uniform and a Gaussian parameter distribution. We train our neural network to determine four key MYTORUS parameters, $N_{H,Z}, N_{H,S}$, power-law spectral index $Γ$, and relative normalization $A_{\rm S}$. The observation-based grid significantly outperforms uniform sampling, achieving predictive accuracy for individual parameters >90% ($N_{H,S}$ and $A_{\rm S}$), 89% ($N_{\rm H,Z}$), and 82% ($Γ$) within $\pm1σ$. For all four parameters simultaneously, predictive accuracy remains high ($\sim$70%). The trained NN ML, ML_MYTORUS, is publicly available with a web interface for fast and reproducible parameter inference from $NuSTAR$ spectra. We illustrate its use via application to NGC 4388. This work shows that SBI offers great potential for future distant x-ray reflection studies in AGN or Galactic x-ray binary spectra.

papers.title: Integrated Generation and Purification of Entangled Coherent States for Non-Gaussian Teleportation
papers.abstract: Entangled coherent states (ECS) provide a powerful non-Gaussian resource for continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, but their generation in scalable architectures remains challenging. We propose an integrated photonic scheme that creates high-fidelity quasi-entangled coherent states (quasi-ECS) from a two-mode squeezed vacuum state (TMSVS) via photon subtraction in a symmetric waveguide trimer. The resulting non-Gaussian entanglement is further enhanced by single-photon catalysis, which purifies the distributed state after transmission through lossy channels. The improvement in conditional teleportation fidelity is accompanied by a reduced heralding probability. Using these purified quasi-ECS resources, we analyze a photon-number-based teleportation protocol and demonstrate high-fidelity transfer of both coherent states and Schrodinger cat states. For the logical cat qubit, we use an orthogonal even/odd-cat basis, measurement-dependent phase corrections, and the success-probability-weighted fidelity over six logical input states. For completeness and benchmarking, we also study the Braunstein-Kimble (BK) teleportation protocol using Gaussian TMSVSs. In particular, the teleportation fidelity for cat states exceeds the benchmark value of 2/3 over a broad range of realistic channel and squeezing parameters. By contrast, the underlying TMSVS performs poorly within the photon-number-based protocol, whereas in the BK protocol it exceeds this benchmark only in a restricted regime of high squeezing and high transmissivity. Our results show that integrated photon subtraction and catalysis enable practical, chip-compatible generation of non-Gaussian entanglement suitable for advanced quantum teleportation and CV quantum networks.

papers.title: Intra-Agent Motion and Inter-Agent Relation Learning for Map-Free Trajectory Prediction
papers.abstract: Trajectory prediction is essential for safe planning and decision-making in autonomous driving. Map-free prediction improves deployment flexibility by removing the dependence on high-definition maps, but it also loses explicit road-topology and lane-connectivity priors. Consequently, the model must recover stable motion cues from short histories while resolving prospective interaction relations without lane-level guidance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a map-free trajectory prediction framework centered on a novel Goal-Conditioned Expert-Routed Transformer (GCERT). A lightweight intra-agent front-end first decomposes projected historical motion features into a smooth trend and a local detail residual through a centered moving average. Component-specific residual projections transform the two signals before a causal temporal Transformer summarizes their recombined evolution. GCERT employs dual-level expert routing: edge-level relation experts generate interaction-specific messages, while node-level state experts adapt the transformation after message aggregation. Predicted motion goals update the node representations and construct prospective relative-geometry and orientation edge features before the final interaction layer, thereby conditioning attention, relation-specific message generation, and state transformation. GCERT therefore determines not only which neighboring agents should be attended to, but also what relation-specific information should be transmitted and how the aggregated node state should be transformed. The resulting representations are decoded into multimodal future trajectories and jointly optimized with trajectory-regression, mode-classification, and goal-prediction objectives.

papers.title: From Strategy Search to Policy Learning: MCTS-Guided Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly power web-facing applications, including conversational assistants and content services, where open user interaction exposes them to diverse safety threats and adaptive attacks. In particular, jailbreak attackers repeatedly reformulate harmful requests to bypass safety alignment. Although existing studies have concentrated on defending dynamic jailbreaks, they often retain discovered attacks as flat samples and discard information about how those attacks were found. In this paper, we introduce MACE, an MCTS-guided adversarial co-evolution framework that turns search into policy-learning signals for both an attacker and a defender. Its search component, GS-MCTS, explores multi-step compositions of rewriting operators and associates discovered attacks with empirical success frequency and path depth. Its optimization component, AC-TGPO, uses these statistics for difficulty-aware group-relative credit assignment and constructs a temporally asymmetric curriculum from current interactions, pairings between the latest attacker and preceding defender, and attacks that survive a defense update. Thus, MACE connects search structure to both within-round policy optimization and cross-round memory, rather than using MCTS only to generate attacks or treating each round as a flat adversarial dataset. Removing difficulty-aware weighting, asymmetric samples, or persistent hard samples increases defense ASR-LR by 3.7 %, 6.0 %, and 5.0 %, respectively. Across evaluated models, the resulting attacker achieves the highest ASR-LR in all six model--dataset settings, while the defender reduces average ASR-LR from 11.9 % for the best baseline to 8.8 %.

papers.title: A physics-constrained neural solver for incompressible flows without labeled data
papers.abstract: We present a physics-constrained neural solver for incompressible flow that requires neither labeled data nor supervised pretraining. The solver enforces incompressibility and boundary conditions (BCs) to strict tolerances. We attribute the limited Reynolds numbers of existing physics-informed approaches to insufficient enforcement of these constraints, on which conventional finite-difference and finite-volume solvers depend. We therefore formulate incompressible flow as a constrained optimization problem within the physics- and equality-constrained artificial neural network (PECANN) framework: the pressure Poisson residual is minimized subject to the momentum equations, continuity equation, and BCs imposed as equality constraints on the primitive variables, while a conditionally adaptive augmented Lagrangian method enforces each constraint. The pressure Poisson objective proves critical. Across all benchmarks, replacing it with the momentum residual fails to converge to accurate solutions under identical architecture and constraint enforcement, which we attribute to the global elliptic coupling of pressure and velocity that local momentum-residual minimization lacks. For advection-dominated flows, we introduce an adaptive vanishing entropy viscosity that stabilizes training while leaving the converged solution unchanged. The solver predicts lid-driven cavity flow up to Re = 7,500 with centerline velocity profiles matching benchmark data, and is further validated on flow over a backward-facing step at Re = 800, 3D unsteady Beltrami flow, and steady and unsteady flow past a circular cylinder under an inflow-outflow configuration, for which an ablation study identifies admissible outlet BCs for velocity and pressure. From a randomly initialized network and without external perturbations, the solver captures the spontaneous onset of periodic vortex shedding in unsteady cylinder flow.

papers.title: BPS Solutions of 4d Euclidean N=2 Supergravity with Higher Derivative Interactions
papers.abstract: We study fully BPS and a broad class of half-BPS stationary configurations of four-dimensional Euclidean N=2 supergravity with higher-derivative interactions. Working within the off-shell conformal supergravity framework of de Wit and Reys (arXiv:1706.04973), we analyse the complete set of Killing spinor equations and obtain the corresponding algebraic and differential constraints. We further derive the Euclidean attractor equations and evaluate the Wald entropy for the fully BPS AdS_2 x S^2 background. For half-BPS stationary configurations, we obtain the generalized stabilization equations expressing all fields in terms of harmonic functions on three-dimensional flat base space, extending the Lorentzian analysis of Cardoso et al (arXiv:hep-th/0009234) to the Euclidean signature. Our results provide a framework for studying supersymmetric saddles and computing the gravitational indices entirely within Euclidean higher-derivative supergravity, without recourse to analytic continuation.

papers.title: Delay-Aware Distributed Multi-Robot Motion Planning
papers.abstract: This paper examines why distributed optimization degrades when multi-robot systems coordinate under realistic communication delays. Using consensus ADMM as a representative framework for generating collision-free, dynamically feasible motion plans in both trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control settings, we show that delay degrades performance structurally: the consensus and dual updates weight stale and current information identically, so staleness enters the optimizer disguised as genuine disagreement and accumulates through the multipliers. Delay-agnostic adaptation (e.g. residual balancing) inherits this contamination and can perform worse than a fixed penalty. We introduce a Delay-Aware ADMM (DA-ADMM) variant that adapts penalty parameters to real-time delay statistics and re-derives the global consensus update as a delay-weighted average, down-weighting stale information in favor of recent updates. Simulations in 2D and 3D show that DA-ADMM improves robustness, success rate, and solution quality over fixed-parameter, residual-balancing, lower-bound, and fixed-constraint baselines. Degradation is therefore governed not by delay length or frequency, but by the optimizer's ability to reason over the age of the information it receives.

papers.title: Lower Bounds on High Moments of Twisted Fourier coefficients of Modular Forms
papers.abstract: For any large prime $q$, $x \leq 1$ and any real $k\geq 2$, we prove a lower bound for the following $2k$-th moment \begin{equation*} \sum_{\substack{χ\in X_q^*}} \Big| \sum_{n\leq x} χ(n)λ(n)\Big|^{2k}, \end{equation*} where $X_q^*$ denotes the set of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$ and $λ(n)$ the Fourier coefficients of a fixed modular form. The bound we obtain is sharp up to a constant factor under the generalized Riemann Hypothesis.

papers.title: Non-commutative crepant resolutions of toric singularities with divisor class group of rank one
papers.abstract: We classify the basic reflexive modules giving toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of Gorenstein toric singularities whose divisor class group has rank one. Their isomorphism classes are parametrized by nonempty proper upper sets in a partially ordered quotient of the class group. Each upper set determines a finite subset called its window, which specifies the divisorial summands. The number of summands in each such module equals the normalized volume of the associated lattice polytope, as conjectured by Van den Bergh. If two upper sets differ by one element, their modules are related by a finite sequence of Iyama--Wemyss mutations. Such sequences connect any two of the classified modules, so all toric NCCRs of a fixed singularity are derived equivalent. We construct higher-dimensional analogues of dimer dual quivers when the associated $d$-dimensional lattice polytope is non-pyramidal. The same window determines a cut of a periodic quiver on the $d$-torus. The cut gives an explicit presentation of the endomorphism algebra by a quiver with relations. For $d=2$, the resulting quiver is dual to a dimer model, a bipartite tiling of the two-torus.

papers.title: Electrokinetic effects on flow and ion transport in charge-patterned corrugated nanochannels
papers.abstract: The phase offset between surface charge modulation and geometric undulations in a corrugated nanochannel provides a tunable mechanism for rectified, diode-like ion transport under purely pressure-driven conditions: reversing the applied pressure gradient selectively activates transport of opposite ionic species, generating a net ionic current whose sign and magnitude are set by the charge-geometry alignment. Fully coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Stokes simulations reveal the underlying two-regime structure: at low driving force (Regime I), throughput is suppressed below the Poiseuille limit by a localized streaming potential that pins counterions within the electric double layer; above a threshold pressure (Regime II), the mechanical force overcomes electrostatic resistance, producing an abrupt, orders-of-magnitude rise in mean velocity. Electroosmotically driven flow undergoes a qualitatively similar but smoother transition. Peak charge selectivity is achieved at near-complete electric double layer overlap and driving forces just below the Regime I-Regime II transition. Random walk particle tracking confirms selective rectification and quantifies the dependence of ion dispersion on surface charge placement across both regimes.

papers.title: All-Gaussian State Discrimination Beyond the Coherent Helstrom Bound
papers.abstract: A core problem in communications is the optimal discrimination of binary-phase-shift-keyed (BPSK) signals. A longstanding goal has been to reach the fundamental quantum limit, known as the Helstrom bound, for BPSK signals encoded in coherent states. However, due to technical constraints, proposals for reaching the bound remain impractical. In this letter we take an alternative approach: using only Gaussian optics - displaced squeezed states and homodyne detection - we achieve discrimination of BPSK signals with error rates below what can be achieved using coherent states and any quantum measurement.

papers.title: Transient Signal Propagation in Heterogeneous Networks under Various Inputs
papers.abstract: Transient signals in neural, biological and technological networks rarely follow a single route. Their strength and timing depend on where the input enters, on the intrinsic dynamics of each node visited, and on the feedforward and recurrent pathways that carry it. Previous theory has clarified important limits of signal propagation, but often for a single input type, averaged network structure, or asymptotic regimes. It has remained unclear how finite heterogeneous networks transform sustained, impulsive, finite-duration and stochastic inputs into node-resolved response timescales. Here, we develop a theory for network dynamics near stable operating states that answers this question. The framework identifies a canonical set of gains and timescales shared across deterministic and stochastic forcing and expresses them through matrix resolvents, spectra and directed walks. In positive, sufficiently damped networks, the walk representation gives a simple physical picture: response strength accumulates multiplicatively along a single path, whereas response time accumulates additively, through local intrinsic time constants. Competing pathways, feedback and inhibition further reshape propagation by amplifying, suppressing, reversing or delaying signals. We derive perturbative criteria that specify when these signatures, and the resulting node rankings, persist beyond the positive regime. Applied to a Wilson--Cowan model of the primate cortex, the theory links structural connectivity, excitatory--inhibitory balance and local biophysical timescales to hierarchical response timescales. Our results provide a mechanistic framework for input-dependent timescales in finite heterogeneous networks.

papers.title: Interpret Policies in Deep Reinforcement Learning using SILVER with RL-Guided Labeling: A Model-level Approach to High-dimensional and Multi-action Environments
papers.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) achieves remarkable performance but lacks interpretability, limiting trust in policy behavior. The existing SILVER framework (Li, Siddique, and Cao 2025) explains RL policy via Shapley-based regression but remains restricted to low-dimensional, binary-action domains. We propose SILVER with RL-guided labeling, an enhanced variant that extends SILVER to multi-action and high-dimensional environments by incorporating the RL policy's own action outputs into the boundary points identification. Our method first extracts compact feature representations from image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution, and then employs RL-guided labeling to generate behaviorally consistent boundary datasets. Surrogate models, such as decision trees and regression-based functions, are subsequently trained to interpret RL policy's decision structure. We evaluate the proposed framework on two Atari environments using three deep RL algorithms and conduct human-subject study to assess the clarity and trustworthiness of the derived interpretable policy. Results show that our approach maintains competitive task performance while substantially improving transparency and human understanding of agent behavior. This work advances explainable RL by transforming SILVER into a scalable and behavior-aware framework for interpreting deep RL agents in high-dimensional, multi-action settings.

papers.title: A Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on non-CMC closed manifolds
papers.abstract: In the paper, we prove the existence of a positive and essentially bounded solution to a Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on a closed manifold with non-constant mean curvature. In particular, the non-constant mean curvature gives rise to supercritical terms in the equation, on top of singular ones. We employ a recent fixed-point argument, which involves sub- and supersolutions. Additionally, we provide several conditions on the coefficients in the equation that prevent the existence of positive classical solutions.

papers.title: Blow-up rate for the subcritical semilinear heat equation in non-convex domains
papers.abstract: We consider the semilinear heat equation $u_t=Δu+|u|^{p-1} u$ in possibly non-convex and unbounded domains. Our main result shows the nonexistence of type II blow-up for possibly sign-changing solutions in the energy subcritical range $(n-2)p<n+2$. This resolves a long-standing open question dating back to the 1980s and also deduces the blow-up of the scaling critical norm.

papers.title: Generalized Centralizers and Polynomial Equivalence of Matrices: Answers to Questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova
papers.abstract:
For $n	imes n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ over a field and a scalar $ω
e0$, let $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\{X:AX=ωXA\}$. If $ω$ is a root of unity of order $q\ge2$, then $\mathcal C_{ω^j}(A)=\mathcal C_{ω^j}(B)$ for all integers $j$ if and only if each of $A$ and $B$ is a polynomial in the other with exponents $\equiv1\pmod q$. Over algebraically closed fields, for $ω
e1$, all $A$, and scalars $\varepsilon
e0$, we describe all $Y$ with $XY=\varepsilon YX$ for all $X\in\mathcal C_ω(A)$. Let $a(μ)$ be the size of the largest Jordan block of $A$ at $μ$, or $0$ if there is none. If $\varepsilon$ is a power of $ω$, all such $Y$ are polynomials in $A$ if and only if $a(ωμ)=a(μ)$ for all $μ
e0$, or this fails only at some $ν$ and at $ω^{-1}ν$, where $A$ has a single largest Jordan block at $ν$ and $a(ων)=a(ω^{-1}ν)=a(ν)-1$. This answers two questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova. If $ω
e1$ has finite order, then for such $A$, $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\mathcal C_ω(B)$ exactly when $A$ and $B$ are polynomials in each other of this form. For all other $A$ some $B$ that is not a polynomial in $A$ satisfies $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\mathcal C_ω(B)$ if the field has more than $n^2+1$ elements. In the $ω$-commuting digraph of Raja and Vaezpour, with an edge from $A$ to $B$ if $AB=ωBA$, vertices with edges to and from the same vertices are twins. Over fields with more than $2n^2+1$ elements we determine the vertices $A$ whose twins are all polynomials in $A$, and describe these twins. We find all $A$, $B$, and $k\ge2$ for which the kernel of $(X\mapsto[A,X])^k$ is the set of $X$ with $[X,[X,\ldots,[X,B]\ldots]]=0$ ($k$ brackets), where $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. Apart from scalar $B$, this happens only in characteristic $
e2$, for $k=2$ and $2	imes2$ matrices that generate the same quadratic extension.

papers.title: The Economics of AI Foundation Models: Openness, Competition, and Governance
papers.abstract: Foundation model developers choose how open to make their models. Greater openness lowers downstream adaptation costs but can also make competing models easier to use. In a two-period model, an incumbent chooses its license fee and openness, a deployer adapts the model for users, and an entrant offers a competing model. Usage builds model-specific experience that lowers the deployer's future adaptation cost, creating a data flywheel that favors continued use of the incumbent. We identify conditions under which optimal openness falls and then rises as learning strengthens. The incumbent moves from full openness and a high fee to restricting openness for retention, then to a low fee that builds enough usage and experience to retain the deployer despite greater openness. A full-openness mandate can induce the incumbent to abandon this low-fee strategy. The higher fee can reduce first-period adaptation despite greater openness. An openness trap arises when this welfare loss exceeds the second-period gain from easier adaptation of the entrant's model. The trap can disappear when experience transfers across models. Full integration eliminates the fee between the incumbent and deployer but commits deployment to the incumbent, potentially forgoing a rival that is cheaper to adapt. Integration raises their joint profit, consumer surplus, and welfare when learning is sufficiently strong, but can lower them when learning is weak. A small usage subsidy can benefit both developers, the deployer, and consumers. It can instead induce a fee increase larger than the subsidy and reduced openness, raising the deployer's net payment per use and adaptation costs. The resulting reduction in adaptation lowers welfare even before subsidy expenditure is deducted. These findings connect AI policy to developers' pricing and openness responses and the portability of deployment experience.

papers.title: A Subspecialty Diagnostic System Powered by Self-Supervised Learning for Cervical Histopathology
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major malignancy in women, with large-scale human papillomavirus-based screening generating a large volume of biopsies and, for advanced cases, surgical specimens, imposing an overwhelming diagnostic burden that necessitates precise histopathological evaluation. Although deep learning shows promise, general foundation models offer a broader reach but remain limited in capturing subspecialty-specific features and task adaptability. We introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, built upon the subspecialized dataset and developed through two synergistic pretraining stages: self-supervised learning on approximately 190 million tissue patches to build a cervical-specific feature extractor, and multimodal enhancement with 2.5 million image-text pairs, followed by diagnostic functions integration and downstream task enhancement. CerS-Path integrates eight functions -- across morphological diagnosis, predictive analytics, and multimodal tasks -- to cover the diagnostic workflow from biopsies to resection specimens. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate improved performance in cervical pathology in female patients, where CerS-Path outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across 26 of 30 diagnostic tasks. Furthermore, in multicenter retrospective and prospective validation across six independent cohorts of women, CerS-Path achieves up to 99% sensitivity for clinically relevant lesion detection with acceptable specificity across sites, highlighting its potential for screening-derived histopathology and suitability for integration into high-volume diagnostic pathways.

papers.title: A polynomial-time algorithm to compute the co-boxicity of block-structured graphs
papers.abstract: The boxicity of a graph $G$ is the minimum dimension $d$ that admits a representation of $G$ as the intersection graph of a family of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Boxicity has applications in ecology and operations research, where it models competition for shared resources. Computing boxicity is an NP-hard problem. Despite considerable theoretical interest, few graph classes are known for which the boxicity can be computed in polynomial time. Following the approach of Cozzens and Roberts (1983), we study directly the boxicity of graph complements, which we call co-boxicity. In this setting, the geometric intersection problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ becomes a graph cover problem involving only complements of interval graphs.
